assurance: Internal written reductions and bounded complete classifications, with exact primary theorem hypotheses. The complete arbitrary-passport classification remains open. No independent replay, formal verification, external mathematical review or priority claim.

declarations.name: Lemma H1. The cycle-incidence tree
declarations.scope: For any minimal full-cycle polynomial tuple, the bipartite incidence graph of sheet vertices and nontrivial cycle vertices is a tree. Cycles within one factor have disjoint supports; whole-factor braiding moves them together. Conversely every such support tree expands to a transposition tree and full-cycle product.

declarations.name: Lemma H2. The invariant block-divisor lattice
declarations.scope: Every invariant block system of a group containing the fixed long cycle P_N is a congruence partition modulo a divisor d of N. The generator congruence test is exact, and the admissible divisor set is a braid-invariant lattice closed under gcd and lcm.

declarations.name: Theorem H3. The quotient and fibre index budget
declarations.scope: For each invariant d-block system of block size b, ind(g_i)=b ind(q_i)+sum_O ind(h_iO). Minimality forces total quotient index d-1 and total fibre-return index b-1. Projection commutes with braids; quotient components and decorated return-cycle types are necessary invariants, without a sufficiency or independent-inner-braid claim.

declarations.name: Theorem H4. Complete classification with two finite branch values
declarations.scope: For all degrees and arbitrary two-factor minimal passports, Q^2 is conjugation by P^-1. Every literal full component is the explicit union of at most2N cyclic conjugates of a pair and its Q image; pure components are cyclic conjugacy classes. Bicolored plane trees with retained cyclic orders classify ordered absolute components; color exchange is added when appropriate for full braids. Centralizer symmetry is retained.

declarations.name: Proposition H5. Standard spin is forced for every odd-order passport
declarations.scope: For every genus-zero polynomial passport whose finite factors all have odd order, the standard spin including infinity is fixed by the cycle types, (-1)^(sum w(g_i)+w(P^-1)). Hence standard spin cannot distinguish its components. This does not classify all central covers or independently prescribed lifted branch data.

declarations.name: Theorem H6. Six primitive components with the same standard spin
declarations.scope: The degree11 passport (3^2 1^5),(3^3 1^2) has six full components, each22 literal tuples over both placements and11 in one ordering. All have the same literal group A11, no nontrivial blocks, the same finite A11 classes and standard spin+1. The degree9 equal-type pair has three full components18,9,9 and four ordered absolute pure components, all group order1512 and spin+1.

declarations.name: Theorem H7. A genus-zero primitive/imprimitive split on fifteen sheets
declarations.scope: The degree15 passport (3^3 1^6),(3^3 1^6),(3 1^12) has exactly two full components: A15 of58725 literal tuples,3915 absolute classes and pure fixed-pattern size19575; C3 wr A5 of75 literal tuples,15 absolute classes and pure fixed-pattern size25. Their cyclic stabilizers have orders1,3; both spins are-1. The imprimitive quotient has d5,b3, quotient index4 and fibre-return index2.

declarations.name: Lemma H8. Refinement can bridge rigid components in a different passport
declarations.scope: All18 single-cycle refinements of the six ordered degree11 rigid representatives lie in one complete3267-tuple refined full braid domain. Exact ordinary braid words are retained. Coalescing recovers each original pair; these words do not connect the original rigid passport because they need not preserve the coalescing constraint.

declarations.name: Proposition H9. The primitive group reduction
declarations.scope: For at least three finite critical values, the only proper primitive polynomial monodromy groups besides Sn,An are the three exceptional PSL3(2),PSL3(3),PSL4(2) cases in degrees7,13,15 and the exact involution passports of Jones–Zvonkin Theorem1.3. This is an imported group reduction, not a general component theorem.

declarations.name: Theorem H10. Imported exceptional-passport component classification
declarations.scope: Imported complete absolute component tables for the three exceptional passports: degree7 sizes21,21 (A7) and7,7 (PSL3(2)); degree13 size35620 (A13) and four13 (PSL3(3)); degree15 all placements size377835 (A15),135 ((S3 wr S5) intersect A15), and15,15 (PSL4(2)). Tuple cyclic stabilizers are trivial. The degree13/15 computational classifications are imported, not independently replayed here.

verification.count_independence: General exterior-power class-character formula rederived in the existing census note and evaluated with exact Fractions. Compared with the quoted Goulden–Jackson expression, preserving fractional class weights such as28/3. Neither random seeds nor the size of one sampled orbit supplies coverage.
verification.spin_convention: A3-cycle lift is (e_a-e_b)(e_b-e_c)/2 in the Euclidean Clifford cover. Products for disjoint3-cycles commute and give the canonical odd-order factor lift. Integer numerators are compared to the adjacent-root lift of P; its Nth power is evaluated by repeated multiplication by two-term vectors, giving the actual central sign.

mathematical_review.scope: Internal audit of subgroup-preserving braids, every regular-cycle block system, exact quotient return budgets, ordered versus unordered branch colors, all six A11 certificate words, nontrivial imprimitive deck symmetry, literal and absolute counts, standard-spin genus restriction and refinement/coalescence scope.

remaining_frontier: The active target remains complete component classification for all genus-zero polynomial passports. H4 resolves two finite values; H2–H3 constrain imprimitive gluing; H5 rules out standard-spin separation in the odd-order genus-zero domain; H6 shows even group+block+spin data are insufficient. Primitive Sn/An components for r>=3 and the joint braid action on lifts above quotient components remain open.
